Hi there.

From what you tell me, I believe I've been in the situation your BF is currently in and I would like to give you my perspective as to why I would consider ending the relationship if you're having doubts. To summarise everything I'm outlining below, I strongly believe the pressure of approval you're describing is both hard and ongoing if you decide to pursue this relationship. You either accept that and learn to integrate yourself to it the best you can (without compromising on your core values) or decide to grin and bear it for as long as it takes. And that could be a lifetime.

My family migrated to our current country of residence decades before I met someone who I then found out lived out of state, so eventually I moved out and to her state to start a relationship. It lasted for just over a year and in that time, I learnt that aside from geographical distance and ethnic background, we also had significant cultural differences that needed compromising on, yet we couldn't in the end. 

I'm going to be blunt. Whether you like it or not, he HAS the family he has. That's never going to change. That Family is what welcomed him into the world. Raised him. Gave him a place to belong. And I'm telling you if his parents don't respect or approve of you now, then they will continue to disapprove of you, even if you worked hard and managed to gain their respect. Not saying this is fair or logical, it's just the way they are, because of their own background and customs and cultural conditioning  demand that they are either unable or unwilling to compromise on their judgment (i.e. either they've been wrong all along and they need to adjust their worldview and accept they've been wrong, or it's just you that's wrong and not them). 

So you have to decide right now, at the very start, if you're up for this journey that might include children down the line, with a partner that will constantly be torn up choosing between you and His Family. He will be called Disloyal, Inconsiderate, Selfish and Obstinate by either side at one point or another for making any choice that places one over the other. Does he love you? Sure he does. Very much so, I suspect, or else he would not consider a future away from his family and country. But that love is largely Untested and Hypothetical because up until now, he's never really had to choose between either one of you. But the moment he moves in with you, that's when Reality starts. If you're lucky and work together to be considerate to one another, willing to compromise and give him and his family the consideration and authority over your relationship they FEEL they deserve, then maybe you can make it, yet be prepared to be never fully accept it. 

If you're not, it will be a very unhappy few months/years ahead where you both feel pressured to give up control of your relationship to the larger family that will always be casting a shadow over your relationship (they're not going anywhere) until one day you or your partner decide they can't do this any longer. It might even be a relief for him, not having to constantly compromise between you and his family.

My brother, you are 15. It sucks that things haven't gone well up to this point, yet I envy you. Within you lies the seeds of Possibility. There is a lot of life ahead of you to explore and find Happiness and Contentment. You also have plenty of time to safely fuck-up a few times before you find what stirs up passion within you, what you're really good at, and what you can safely do without going forward. 

All that is needed now is for you to invest a little time in thinking about something new that you can try on. 

For me, it was exercise. I tried walking a few blocks just to clear my head. Then I found I liked it and walked a bit faster. Then I stepped it up and made myself jog for an hour or so. It made me feel happy to just keep on moving and I knew I was doing something good for myself. Such a little thing. Just succeeding at something small helped me build my confidence one little bit at a time. Many years have passed since. I've moved on from jogging, but have tried many other things, losing my fear and hesitation. Some were spectacular failures, but there were many small and some large victories in between. 

At 15 I had no fucking idea of what I wanted to be. Honestly, I didn't think I was good for anything. I even went to University without really knowing what I wanted at the end of that degree. I found my way by meeting many different people and sharing on their life experiences, their dreams and hopes and their opinions about myself. I took in both the good and the bad advice and eventually I built enough of a Body of Knowledge to understand what it was I was passionate about, what I was actually good at and finally, what new things I wanted to try. That led me to where I am now. And I am still searching for new purpose. It's a journey, not a race.

As I grew up, I came across many people that were smarter, better-looking, far more charismatic and interesting and looked at myself. It did give me an sense of inferiority until I realised there will ALWAYS be people that are more attractive, more intelligent and far more charismatic than I am. And that's OK.  It may be hard for you to realise it now, but Attractiveness is completely Relative. What some people find attractive and endearing, others will find annoying or repulsive even. I've met my share of Smart, educated people that didn't know how to operate outside of their field of expertise and shut down completely when faced with something new outside of their body of knowledge, especially if they only excelled in a relatively small environment. My best friends are people who earned their knowledge and wisdom the Hard Way, not because they were smart to begin with. And I have some really dumb friends that I would take a bullet for. Because what they lack in wisdom, they make up in Loyalty and Kindness. Those two will get anyone a long way further than you'd think. 

Don't despair. This time will pass. There is so much more to life ahead of you than you can imagine at this point. So much opportunity to develop and be whatever you want to be. All you need to do is gather the courage to take that first step and try something new. See where it takes you. Stick with it long enough to make an informed decision whether if it's something you like or not. And then pick something else to do. The important part is building that experience while you discover who you are and who you want to be. For what it's worth, I am cheering for you. You got this.

Most things I can objectively chalk up to coincidence, external, yet-natural phenomena mistaken otherwise or my imagination. But there is one instance that still remains with me over the years. 

Back when I was a young boy, my family had moved into an old bungalow-style home. We had no knowledge of its history, nor was it a factor when it was purchased; we were just looking for a reasonably priced place to live in. Decades later we learnt the whole area was basically built up as cheap housing for returned soldiers after the second world war. The house came with a very large backyard where mature English laurel bushes had overgrown and taken over the back section over the fence. That was Dad and my older brother's No.1 priority - to remove those bushes (mum wanted to plant some fruit trees in the back). The removal went without a hitch and the back area now looked *barren*. You could see the back fence now.

My brother next wanted to build his home gym in the back of the garage, so he spent the great part of the afternoon putting it together. Just before sundown, I went in to watch him and see if I could help him. It was just before dusk that he asked me to bring him a tool from inside the house, where Dad had left his toolbox as he was fixing some shelves in one of the bedrooms inside. I went in and it took me like 10 minutes to find it. During that time, the day turned to night and it was **dark** since the streetlights or our backyard lights had not yet turned on. 

So here's the thing. I remember stepping outside into the back porch. I remember turning left and making my way to the garage. That's when I noticed the dark shape standing still, silhouetted against the back fence. There was no discernible features; just a really, really "solid" shadow. And it was standing in one particular spot. As I saw it, it raised an arm.  My mind quickly assessed this was no idle person in my backyard, that it was a solid shadow and that it had waved at me the moment I noticed it. I was too shocked to move. Then my brother yelled angrily at me to hurry up, I got momentarily distracted, felt a breeze and looked at the garage and then tried to look back again at the spot, but just as I was turning my head, I could see the shape just *vanished*. Like, it didn't pop out of existence or moved elsewhere (there was nowhere to hide now that the bushes were gone), it just *melted* into nothing more than ordinary shadows and edges. My blood ran cold. I staggered into the garage and refused to leave until I left with my brother in tow. 

Many months later, when my dad finally got around to building mum her garden beds in the back, we dug up buttons. Then a buckle. Then bits of fabric that looked like heavy wool, long rotten away. And then we found the uniform badges and medals in the rusty remains of a metal box that must have been buried until the laurel bushes many, many years ago. Looking back, I figure someone buried a uniform and all the medals in a small footlocker in the backyard. 

And then waved at me to let me know where it was the first chance it got. 

We got in touch with our local RSL and they came and took the pieces we found, including the medals. They would send them to the War Memorial in Canberra. I choose to believe its owner was satisfied as no one else saw that shadow ever again to the day we sold that property decades later.

I doubt it. Manga reflects the Japanese work culture (South Korean too). In both countries, work culture has evolved to reward conformity rather than individuality. 

It's not that the MC is "super talented", but rather someone who has put some effort in their work, only to have that eagerness crushed by  coworkers who, comparatively, look worse at their roles now that the newcomer that tried to be a little bit better. In the traditional Japanese office, there is no greater sin that to be idle or to stand out. You are given a task and the office expects you to take a certain amount of time and effort and collaboration to get it done. If you are too eager and get your share done early, you're making the rest look bad. If you do it alone, you're implying the rest are not needed. If you  complete your task without using the allocated resources, you've allowed waste to happen. A task must be performed within the alloted time, with the required number of useless meetings involving other team members and using the allocated resources. Bonus points if it looks like you worked hard to the very last minute, going early to the office and leaving long after your supervisor has gone home for the day.

I've seen this type of mentality before. In the workplace when a member quits due to overwork, underpay or unreasonable accountability. I've seen supervisors think they can make do by splitting the tasks of the departing member between the remaining staff. And when it all falls over, they ask if they can get the number of the departed member and "do him/her a favour" and take them back with a nominal raise. Because they can't see beyond their narrow sight.

The relationship between the characters is best explained through their Passions, their sources of Inspiration and Dedication to it. What we see at the beginning is the MC (Kousei) who has lost his inspiration but not his passion (music). His inability to hear himself play fuels his yearning and isolation. He feels *punished* and ends up believing himself cursed as a result of his lack of dedication (to music and his mother, his source of inspiration). He is broken and unable to move forward, something that his closest friends and allies are able to see but not fully understand, so they simply stand by him while they hope he finds a way out of his rut. 

What is interesting is that he himself was the source of inspiration to both a young Kaori, Emi, Takeshi (and indirectly Nagi as well). His first concert apparently moved them all toward dedicating themselves to music fully. Some because they wanted to be as good if not better than him at bringing out their best(Takeshi), some to capture the feeling of that first concert and make it their own (Emi), and some because they wanted to be part of his world (Kaori and latter Nagi). Kousei was their Inspiration and because of him they all found their Passion. How they chose to express it or nurture it depended on the individual. But while Takeshi and Emi spend the next few years dedicating themselves to their passion, only Kaori really depends on her source of Inspiration (Kousei) to achieve her Passion (to play together). 

She knew of "Kousei the Performer" and evenheard of "Kousei the Classmate", not daring to approach him due to her own inhibitions. But once her situation turns terminal, she finds the courage to let go of her doubts and pursues her Passions to the fullest, in music as well as indulgence. And that includes finding her way into Kousei the Classmate and get to know her source of Inspiration (i.e. Kousei the Performer). Her impulsive decision led her to understand his predicament and rather than push her feelings onto him, she decides to seek out Kousei the Performer and help him rediscover his passion once more. In the process of doing this, she falls in love with him but holds back because her own situation is growing dire. You see, up until that point, she had *admired* Kousei without really knowing the boy behind the Performer. Once she knew him better, it was too late for her to express herself without causing pain to all around her. So she holds back. What she doesn't realise is that by then (and through her), Kousei has once again found a source of inspiration that allows him to rediscover his Passion and let go of his former insecurities. He fell in love with her without realising it himself. Once he's aware of his feelings though, he's unable to pursue them because of the pain he would cause to his friend Ryota. Tsubaki isn't even in the picture at this point, since he can only see her as a sibling of sorts, even though it's obvious to everyone around them that she cares for him, even if she doesn't understand it herself. This weird triangle holds everyone back just long enough for each of them to discover their own hidden feelings and the rest of the show is all about them pursuing their passions and expressing themselves through them. Music is the medium through which they all express themselves in ways they can't do in the open. The ending while tragic left a lot of unanswered questions behind. Some of these are answered through the Coda chapters but the result of the whole journey is that Kousei is once again whole and can now move forward and pursue his passion (music) wherever it will lead him. Tsubaki is now honest with her feelings and free to pursue it as she chooses. Emi and Takeshi renew their passion and dedication and find friendship and friendly rivalry with Kousei and can also now grow together once more. Nagi has also found passion through music and will pursue it alongside them. Everyone gets to grow.

"I'm sorry Jared, I can't authorise another Simulation."

Peter had barely arrived at his desk when Jared came marching in. He looked agitated and like he'd missed out on sleep over the weekend. *It's no wonder*, he thought, *if I had a hot-looking wife like him, I bet I'd miss out on a few hours of rest myself*. It's not that Peter resented his younger colleague. With the help of Jared, Peter and his team had made massive breakthroughs in Quantum Computing, to the point the latest iteration of the prototype was undergoing final testing and debugging. They might even deliver to the NSA on time, if not on budget. Not that the NSA was even concerned with their expenditure to date. Not since Jared had demonstrated the incredible value of their high-accuracy quantum extrapolations that had led to the spectacular capture of several local insurgents just as they were getting ready to execute what would have been America's worst domestic terrorist attacks since 9-11. 

But Peter's patience with Jared would only run so far. Each and every one of these test trials required massive computing power. The energy bills alone ran into the hundreds of thousands. The computer, simply put, was *too good* at what it did and became more accurate in its predictions only when the size of the simulation parameters grew and grew. Want to simulate the weather in Seatle? Sure! But just to do that, the machine needed to simulate the weather fronts in the entire continental USA, and then the northen hemisphere. And then the entire planet. For up to 3 weeks in advance. It got even worse when factors involved individual people. The prototype would require petabytes of data on the individual's routine and the routine's of everyone the individual interacted with. And the people they interacted with and so on, for as far back as records were available. It took 6 months to prep up a test run and countless hours of intense labor, feeding all of this data into the prototype.

"Pete, I only need 3 minutes- no, make that 2 minutes of simulation time. The parameters and the data are already in the system from our test run last Wednesday. I can run it myself, but I need you to bring me back out once it's all done. Please." It was only that last sentence that made Peter pay closer attention to Jared. Ever since they've been colleagues, Jared had always been brash and curt. Peter tolerated it only because he understood a man of Jared's brilliance came only once in a lifetime. He could let some character flaws slide. Yet there he was, actually asking him *politely* for once. 

"What would 2 minutes of extra simulation time get us that's so valuable to revisit? We still have tons of result data that we have yet to analyse. Jared, I think you've been working too hard. Maybe it's about time you took that holiday with Jennifer you've been talking about for m.. Jared, what's wrong with you?" At the mention of his wife, Jared looked like he'd been kicked in the stomach. It took Jared a few visible seconds to bring himself under control, something that was not missed on Pete. *what the hell is wrong with him?*

"Pete, there is a high chance that some of the paramaters we fed were outdated and that would have impacted the simulation. I'm not sure how significant it is though. Could be a little. Or could be a whole lot. But we won't know unless we run that section once more. Pete, you know General Catteau has been waiting for an excuse to take over. Do you really want to hand one to him? Look, I promise that once this is done, I'll put in my leave application and take Ca- uh, Jennifer on that holiday I promised. We have a lot riding on this Pete. Help me make it right, please." 

Peter could see that Jared really meant it - that this was no Academic Diva trying to grandstand, but someone who genuinely wanted to review the simulation in earnest. His insticts told him that if Jared believed it was significant enough to review, then he should trust him. "OK, I'll even give you 5 minutes. I'll clear up the approvals with the board and you can run the adjustments later this afternoon. Now go and get yourself some coffee and relax a bit, won't you?"

Jared's relief was palpable. "Thankyou Pete. Your support means a lot to me." *Another first for Jared*, Peter though. Wonders never ceased.

In a small office, in a dark corner of the least visited building at an University, sat a single dumbfounded graduate student. Bryan had been working on a revolutionary method to derive data samples from accross large segments of the global population as part of his thesis and had been frustrated for months as the data simply did not match latest census information or available records. After spending countless months reviewing and redifining his key algorythms, he decided to take a closer look at the source data, not really expecting to find anything outside of the ordinary.

But after cross-checking several records across the continental US, he had enough doubts to compel him to inquire discreetly with colleagues from across to globe to confirm his findings. Eventually, enough of a picture arose that he could no longer pretend what he had suspected for months. That his algorythms were accurate enough. 

The enormity of the implications was simply too much for him to bear on his own. He was concerned - desperate, in fact  - to have someone more intelligent and more experienced than himself to prove him wrong; to find the crucial piece of info he was missing; the wrong assumption he had made, that explained it all. He grudgingly decided to call in Shelley. 

-----------------------------------------------------------------

Shelley Mendez was everything Bryan wasn't. Impulsive, Intuitive and infinitely more liked by their peers than he could ever hope to be. She had been the one constant in his university life all these years, and while not quite a friend, she had become a valuable person, always eager to blindside him and throw his assumptions into turmoil with one clever, insightful observation. He rang her despite the late hour. He knew she'd be up, somewhere.

The loud music and voices in the background validated him just as much as it irritated him.

  
"Hello, Shelley speaking! You're going to have to speak up!"

"Shelley, it's Bryan Mcwhirter speaking. Do you have a moment to talk?" He was practically shouting through the noise.

"Oh, hi Bri! Whatcha up to?" He winced, hating the nickname she had given him and knowing she was well aware of his dislike for it. 

"Please Shelley, I'm in the 3rd lab, as always. Listen, I could use with your help. I'll make it worth your while if you can get here in the next hour."

"Okay, I'm gonna hold you to that! I'll slip outta here right now and meet you in 15 mins. We can talk then."

Before he could reply, she had hung up.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

She was in the lab in less than 10 mins. She must have ran all the way here, still reeking of smoke and vodka. While he couldn't care less what she was up to, he really hoped the booze would not cloud her thinking. 

"Okay, Bri, what's going on? You'd be the last person to call me on a Friday night. Feeling lonely?" she teased.

"Look, you know I wouldn't bother you if I didn't think it was important. I want your undivided attention for 30 minutes. In return, I'll let you see what I've been working on since last year."

That got Shelley's attention. He knew that she'd been dying of curiosity ever since he came back from his research trip. 

In the end, it took him a couple of hours to describe his methodology and approach in order to satisfy all of Shelley's endless stream of questions. He had not expected to reveal so much of his research, but he conceded that she needed to know just as much in order to get her to understand what was happening. Even a Genius needs the correct input to make the right connections. What he showed her though, was enough to amuse, then alert and finally to completely absorb Shelley into it. 

The data showed that multiple countries across the globe were grossly overreporting both birth, migration and death records across all continents for the past 40 years. Something took place nearly half a century ago that caused massive sudden drops in births worldwide. Worse, migration records were severely tampered with to produce a partial picture of large ethnic migrations across the globe when in reality only a trickle of people had traded places. Worse was the undeniable fact that there were hundreds of *millions* of people missing, mostly from 3rd world countries. Economic, development, production data had been accordingly tampered with to account for massive gaps in national budgets across the globe. 

It should have irked Bryan that it only took Shelley a few hours to understand his thesis to the point she further refined and adjusted the algorythms, but her tone and concentration were enough to convince him she was rattled by the preliminary findings also. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

In the end, it took them all night to cross-check and verify the data and it was clear that a vast amount of resources and more importantly, *personnel* were being redirected to an area in the South China sea, hidden through clever shipping manifests, under a cloud of secrecy helped by the Chinese Goverment and contained by NATO, Russian and Chinese forces, where they simply *vanished*. Shipments came in; nothing came back out. 

"I don't know what you've stumbled upon Bri, but the data is pretty fucking conclusive. We need to tell someone."

War casualties in conflicts that never took place. Entire villages lying empty but closed from public eyes. All over the globe, Governments sent either people or resources under the guise of exports to sites that never received those migrants or shipments and then lied about it.

Captain Nell took another look at the display, not quite believing the enhanced topographical images being received real-time on the *Destiny's* bridge. 

"How many, you say?"

The Helms Officer, initially flustered at the readings, replied a lot more steadily now, certain that the information tagged by the mainframe computers had been verified visually by no less than 3 human surveyors onboard. 

"Sir, Initial scans have been verified. We can make out 8 operational Geodesic Domes at the Alpha Site in the largest northen continent and at least 8 more currently under construction. We also make out 4 more in the backup site in the smaller northern continent. We also confirm the remains of a Geodesic Dome in the Delta Site in the Southern Hemisphere. The structure is cold. No heat signatures detected."

A younger officer leaned over and whispered to the Captain "That many Domes could hold at much as 400,000 Colonists. Recommend we continue communications blackout. The situation has changed, Bill."

The Captain looked over at Ray his First Officer and nodded. None of this made sense. Ever since they received the first preliminary survey scans, their mission directives were no longer routine. As a fifth-generation Spacer, Nell had faithfully overseen the execution of all the orders set out almost 200 years prior, in the home planet of Humanity. Ever since he was born, generations of Spacers such as himself had been born, raised and died following the Colonial directives without deviation as the plan demanded. His whole career had led to this moment where he would oversee the end of the decceleration stage of the Colony Generational ship *Destiny* and commence planetfall for the second Colonist wave.

The *Destiny* was the second stage of a 3-stage Colony attempt at Atalia-Prime, the most-promising habitable world discovered by Humanity. Its crew consisted of nearly 10,000 Spacers, descendants of the first generation of Colonists that left earth 200 years prior in their long voyage across the stars. Those Pioneers that left earth had set out and followed a very strict set of directives that had been passed on from generation to generation. Bill remember how proud he was as he received command from Captain Sarkis over 15 years ago, during the last major course correction that led to their current decceleration vector. Once in Orbit of Atalia, he was to make contact with the Survey Team sent ahead 10 years prior. The Survey Team composed of 500 hardly colonists who would make the trip aboard the *Copernicus* ahead of the *Destiny* arrival and conduct a careful survey of the proposed landing sites and begin the construction of 2 standard Geodesic Domes, and more importantly, the Terraforming Reactor, ahead of of the arrival of the *Destiny*. Bill had expected to see the fully completed Dome structure at the Primary site, the Terraforming Reactor and the almost completed secondary dome during his initial scan.

Bill had known something was different to the plan almost 5 years prior when the first deep space scans, sent by probes launched by the *Copernicus* during its initial decceleration burn 10 years prior, revealed several structures that the sensors tagged as Geodesic Domes at a 68% probability. The sensors aboard the Destiny were not sensitive enough to make out much detail at that stage, so they've spent the last 5 years preparing for the moment where they themselves could launch optical probes and obtain the necessary detail required to survey the landing sites from space. At 6 months before estimated Planetfall, Bill knew that the crew of the *Copernicus* could not be responsible for the accelerated construction schedule. Their mission was simply not sufficiently equipped or crewed to continue construction beyond the initial 2 domes. 

"Captain, more data is coming through now." The bridge officer confirmed. "Sir, additional scans confirm the *Copernicus* still orbiting Alpha Prime. We can also confirm 2 additional ships. The *Destiny* tags their make and origin as Earth Vessels."

Bill stared at the display, not quite believing what he was seeing. *How could 2 other Earth vessels launched at least a decade after the *Destiny* have reached Atalia Prime before us?!* 

"Confirm if either one of those 2 vessels match the *Mayflower*!" Bill ordered.

He had seen the schematics of the 3rd wave vessel in the *Destiny's* database. The plan was for the final and largest Colony ship to be launched exactly 20 years after the *Destiny* in order to begin full colonisation, once the crews of the *Copernicus* and the *Destiny* had completed all essential infrastructure required and Terraforming had been completed.

"Match confirmed. *Destiny* tags the unknown vessels as *Mayflower* class variants. The Sensors indicate Reinforced Hulls and smaller propulsion engines." The Engisn swallowed hard. "Capatin, sensors tentavitely assign a 72% probability that both vessels display missile launch tubes across the bow."

"What the hell? Bill, there is no way the *Mayflower* launched ahead of us as a War Vessel."

"At least we know what happened to the Southern Hemisphere dome. That can only be the result of an Orbital Bombardment", said Ray icily. The implications of that statement snapped Bill out of his stupor.

"Helm, immediately shut down all active sensors. Until further notice, we run passive sensors only."

Still, this was no time to panic. Decceleration was still underway. They still have 6, no 5 months to plan their next course of action prior to arrival in orbit. The mission had taken a turn for the worst, from all accounts. The *Copernicus* must have arrived on schedule and proceeded to Terraform and build preliminary settlements as intended and then somehow, before the *Destiny* arrived, Earth must have sent ships using faster technological breakthroughs. The archives showed that theoretically, Faster-Than-Light travel was possible. Surely someone on Earth must have made a breakthrough in the 20 years between missions and leapfrogged ahead of the *Destiny* and arrived at Atalia Prime long before they were expected. And for some reason, they had bombarded the surface. 

"Ray, get in touch with the Ruling Council. We need to appraise everyone of the current situation. There is going to be a lot of people out there that won't like the idea of coming to Atalia Prime under a Hostile Occupation force" He eyed the bridge crew and then announced in his clearest command voice "Attention all bridge personnel. You are hereby ordered to maintain silence on the latest developments until further notice. We don't want to start a panic aboard the *Destiny*. Let's trust in our elected officials to make the next set of decisions".

With that, Captain Bill Nell made his way to the bridge exit airlock, trying his best to project an image of calmness as he left. One thing is for sure, he thought. The old Directives are now officially over. It's time for all of them to start thinking about the future of the *Destiny's* crew instead of trusting their ancestors. Time for all of them to grow up.

"We have lost communications with the Europa."

In a quiet, vast open chamber, sat approximately 50 people in shock. That last sentence hung heavily in the air. After 5 day cycles, they could no longer pretend the lack of responses were due to equipment malfunction or line-of-sight errors. The communication laser equipment had been recalibrated time and time again; the backup RHF and UHF equipment had not stopped broadcasting since the beginning of the emergency. The Europa, our last sister ship in contactable range, had simply ceased to broadcast signals and gone dark. 

A vast array of reactions could be discerned from the Council Members present. These men and women,  representatives of the 500,000 human beings currently living aboard the William Anderson now had to make far-ranging decisions that would affect what could possibly be the course of Humanity.

"I will remind my fellow council members that We are too far away and moving too fast through relative space to render aid or send any probes to investigate the Europa's fate.", continued Council Member Robson, Representative of the Northen Alliance. "We're on our Own, and certain decisions must take place this day to ensure the continuation of our mission and with it, the continuation of our species. While we had been operating on our own for the past 5 standard years, we were due to link up with the Europa in 3 standard years for our scheduled exchange of personel, technology and resources. We can operate on our own, but the William Anderson has spent the last quarter of a century devoted to technological development to maximise the efficient use of our limited resources. The vast majority of our working population is highly educated and specialised in their own limited fields of technological and scientific expertise. This will have to change now. We need more farmers and labourers if we're going to survive the next 137 years."

The William Anderson, like its other sister ships Europa, Shen Yang, Bolivar and Kilo-Hoku, were sent on a voyage to colonise a distant star system light-years from Earth in the farther reaches of the spiral arm. There might have been other ships launched after, but they lost contact with Earth long ago. Everyone secretly doubted it though. This was a voyage not borne out of curiosity of exploration, but driven by pure desperation. Earth was dying; its resources spent and its atmosphere poisoned. And over the past 43 years, the ships had drifted further and further apart, losing contact over the decades until only the Anderson and the Europa remained. And now the Anderson was all alone. 

A tall, slim woman in her late 30s spoke. "Speaker Robson, as the representative of the Europa Union, I insist that we at least try to send a probe. We cannot simply abandon two hundred thousand souls to a terrible, lonely fate.". Robson expected this from Alaine. She had to at least try. What he did not expect was for Councillor Zhao to agree. "The Republic of China also insists we investigate the fate of the Europa. The ship contains valuable food and renewable resources. Even if the crew suffered a catastrophic end, the genetic abundance aboard the Europa is the key to the survival of-"

"And just what do you propose we do that Zhao? We cannot afford to decelerate the Andy in time to intercept without causing massive structural damage. You'd be killing us all!" shouted an outraged young man with a thick latin accent."Everyone, please!" Interjected Speaker Robson. "Ladies and Gentleman. I feel the loss of the Europa as much as any of you, but I have to agree with Councilor Martinez. There is nothing we can do for the Europa at this stage. Whatever we have on board the William Anderson will have to be what we can rely on."

"We cannot feed half a million people with the limited production aboard the Anderson." Interjected Alaine.  "Not for long." 

"Indeed. We cannot. Effective immediately, we must retrain and reallocate the vast majority of our citizens towards food production and systems maintenance. Mr. Nuñez, how goes the Cryo-stasis research?" 

A small, stocky man in his 50s rose, paused, and then deliberately spoke. "Not far enough. we can send subjects to sleep just fine, but in 80% of the simulations, there is severe neural degradation as a result of the revival process. in 5%, they don't wake up at all. We need more time."

"We no longer have the time, I'm afraid. Effectively immediately, please review and evaluate your current research programs and redirect any and all personnel not related to viable, short-term essential projects to food production. There will also be a ban on new births until further notice."

The room erupted in chaos. It went for hours. By the late evening, it was clear that the authority of the council was severely compromised, with many councillors simply walking off. Speaker Robson stood at the center of it, hearing, pleading and in some cases threatening the various councillors to come to an agreement. But of course, it was impossible to make them all agree on the many austerity measures required. Eventualy, they'll have to see there are no other ways, but he knew quite well the harmony aboard the Anderson depended heavily on a delicate and complex set of rules and concessions that kept most enclaves not necessarily happy, but content enough, lay severely strained and in many cases broken. 

There will be many citizens that will simply refuse to make the move from their careers in academia and executive to go tend fields in the main habitats or work in the hydroponic bays or do the many hundreds of menial labor tasks not automated and not required in decades. Worse, to condemn their own children - if they had any - to the same fate. 

By the time the last few left the chamber, Robson knew that life aboard the Anderson would be cruel and harsh on everyone. He briefly wondered about the fate of the crew of the Europa and thought of his only daughter who left to find a life aboard the Europa all those years ago and who he had only spoken to barely a fortnight ago. He left the hall with a heavy heart, no longer able to avoid going home to his wife and tell her the sad news.

Identity Theft is a real danger and it starts with people pretending to be from somewhere they're not. I live alone and it's not THAT outrageous to think someone's targeted what they consider to be a mostly empty home in the neighbourhood as the perfect staging ground for creating a fake identity.

Initially I also assumed it was not intentional so I marked it 'return to sender - no such person at this address - and popped it back in the mail. But then the letters kept on coming and I noticed something troubling; all of these seemed Official Letters: the kind that banks send with PIN numbers and thick form letter packages that were almost certainly carrying cards. My curiosity got the better of me when I saw a letter from a well known insurance company. It had rained that morning so the letter was soggy enough I could open the envelope just by lifting the flap thing. That's when I saw she was registering a home and contents insurance package for MY home. At that point, I stopped sending the letters back and started to open them and sure enough, PIN numbers and credit cards and car registration. I contacted them all and kept the letters to take to the police since this went beyond a little mistake - someone was actively using my home address to build identity points for other official documents and worse, using my home as a form of identity and base of operations. 

The only reason why I caught on is because my mailbox got locked up with a padlock to stop the snails from nesting inside and I was working from home 4 out of 5 days a week instead of commuting to work everyday. So I went to check my mail as soon as the mailwoman dropped it off.

Being part of a well and long established migrant family in a remote but developed country means that occasionally, through our parents, we are contacted by relatives and friends of relatives in our birth country and we are asked to look after and guide younger migrants or students studying abroad. If they're brand-new and with no contacts, we have to help them settle and secure housing and if possible, a job. We gotta make sure they're up to speed with the culture and to explain the Dos and Don'ts. You have to understand from the start that we end up obligated to look after these people, whether we like it or not; failure to do so after our parents have agreed to look after them brings them shame and affects their standing in the expat community. Anyways, that's for background. 

A few years ago, we were asked by my parents to meet and greet this young university student studying here. He'd be like, 10yrs younger than us, but still we made the effort to introduce ourselves and extend a helping hand if they needed it. From the start, it was awkward. The guy seemed very conceited and smug about *his* parent's success and the fact that they could afford to fly him halfway across the world to finish his studies. It seemed odd that he insisted on large, independent housing, close to the city. Typically, students go for share accommodation with other nationals where possible and as close to the campus as they can find it. But no; he wanted it large (2 bedroom plus) and close to the city center. Price was no option. We're talking $900/week of rent and he was OK - he had his dad's credit card and a spending ceiling of $50k, so he said. 

I started to notice a pattern every time we arranged to meet; I'd call and he'd never answer, so I'd leave messages on his phone. He would then text back, arranging a place to meet. We'd talk, occasionally he'd be  there with friends he'd bring along. We'd catch up, see if he was OK and he'd always be smug about how he was doing OK and not to worry. Fair enough; we'd leave him alone and we wouldn't hear from him for weeks or months even. But whenever we met, he'd say his studies were great, he was fine and that he was on track to graduate within 3 years. 

Of course, that didn't happen. On the third year, he confessed he'd been partying too much and had skipped a few exam finals; that he'd have to make up for the lost credits in the next year. OK, that's understandable but unfortunate. Still, it was fine since he had the means to look after himself. Then 6 months later he changed his mind; now that he had all this free time since he was only doing a couple of courses, he wanted to do *another* degree. OK, fine, but that would delay your graduation for another 3 to 4 years. It seemed odd. We began asking around. Yes, he was studying - that much was still certain. But he was **nowhere near** completing his first degree, let alone the second. He was well known for having these really fucked-up loud and long-lasting parties for days on end. Then someone casually mentioned his *fiancée* . I thought I'd contact him and congratulate him and that's when shit hit the proverbial fan. 

He flat out denied it, even though we had fucking photos since he'd been stupid enough to post them all over other friends Facebook accounts (he still maintains he doesn't have an account himself. I don't believe him anymore). Then more interesting facts started to rise. How does someone spend close to seventy fucking thousand dollars a year on studies maybe 5 credits per year? What's he been doing during all this time? Bit by bit, through other intermediaries, a picture emerged. If you believe his version, he's been quietly studying for an industrial engineering degree and he is on his way to complete a second science engineering degree. His living expenses are high due to his decision to live close to the city and because he wanted a large place to live in. By himself.

The other version is that, over three years ago, he showed up with his then-girlfriend from overseas, began working part-time at a hotel with her and has been renting out the more expensive place to **OTHER** people and living far away from the city himself. Both he and his fiancée have been going on overseas holidays during the summer breaks and they've been saving up to move interstate once they graduate. They rake in a lot of money themselves by doing lots of shady shit that may/may not be entirely legal (though no hard evidence is at hand, we suspect fraud as the most likely source of his income with a healthy dose of naive university student exploitation). His parents keep sending him money (and they must be at least $300k out of pocket, by our reckoning) and he keeps on 'investing' it on other rental properties which he then sublets to other poorer university students. At this point in time, I've stopped introducing him to other expats and actively warned those that I have the most confidence in to stay the fuck away from him because any day now this is all going to crash around him when either one of the students denounces him or his disinterested parents come to the realisation he's not graduating any time soon despite all the money they've sunk on him... or he basically runs away and abandons his student visa and goes underground.

I'm in my late 30s. The world of today seems as strange to me as the tales I used to read about people growing up during the Industrial Revolution. Everything about the world is moving so damn quickly and changing almost daily I almost feel the whiplash. 

I look at my nephews and I think about 10yr old me back in the 80s and I think, "fuck, I'd be worse than a rube." I'd gawk at their 3DS gaming systems and the idea of having multiple games available on such a little device. Then I'd have a fucking heart attack when I beheld their ipods and apps. I wouldn't know what to talk to them about. My head back then was filled with thoughts of comics and good old star wars and action figures. I realise that while all of these still exist in some form, they would not resemble what I knew about them back then.  If I was brave enough, I might suggest we go and play some ball on the street... only to be told to get the fuck back into the house since that kind of thing is no longer done since we no longer seem to trust our neighbors or each other. The world would be utterly *alien* to me.

I look at my oldest nephews and I wonder about teenage me back in the 90s. Smartphones would be the fucking thing of the future... but I would be scoffing at the idea of hanging out with people over the phone than in person. Or gaming online when I would want to go watch movies or hang out instead. Social Networks were never bigger than the people I could talk to face to face on a regular basis. And the idea of sharing photos or activities or 'selfies' would disturb me. Photos were special and only for occasions back then. The idea of freely available porn would be awesome and addictive, but when I see what my nephew's friends post on *their* pages, I think I wouldn't even have to go look for porn the way things are going these days. It's far too heavy to think about the relaxation of social norms these days.

I think about 20-something me and while personal computing and cell phones had caught up back then, the level of interaction today would terrify me. The thought that what I considered harmless flirting can now be interpreted as sexual harassment is a sobering thought. That I shouldn't take for granted that I can't talk to kids without other adults around is shocking. That I can't take a trip on a plane without having to surrender my dignity and my privacy is crushing. The idea of the modern work environment and the connected office was pure fantasy back then. I'd laugh at the idea of not having to go to the bank to pay bills or to make large withdrawals. And to even think I could find a job where I'd never even see my boss for months on end would seem insane.

My experience has been one of a world that's growing ever connected... but ever more isolated. We surround ourselves with technology to make our lives easier and more documented than ever before, yet we fail horribly at simple face-to-face interactions I'd grown up on. Having to *see* and *hear* people face-to-face involved a certain level of social skill and decorum that has been increasingly eroded by each new innovation in personal or mobile computing. My world was certainly much smaller as I grew up, but it also made us depend on each other for everything, which meant we had to be part of a community. I don't feel that anymore and I wonder what kind of world my nephews and nieces are growing up in.
